To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of the cancer hallmarks markers Aldh1, EpCAM, and Survivin in colorectal cancer is associated with clinical outcome.
the combined expression of Aldh, Survivin and EpCAM is a strong and independent prognostic marker for survival and recurrence in colorectal cancer patients.

the combination of Aldh1 and Survivin expression, or the combination of EpCAM and Survivin, is a strong prognostic factor for overall survival in CRC, with hazard ratios of 5.3 and 4.8, respectively (P<0,001).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the clinical value of a combined analysis of Aldha1, Survivins, and EpCAM in colorectal cancer patients.
the identification and validation of a novel biomarker panel for the prediction of the clinical course of patients with CRC.
the clinical value of combined analysis, rather than the individual value of each marker, and might be useful in clinical decision making.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of all three markers should be combined to assess the clinical outcome of patients.
the expression of Ald1 and Survivin, but not EpCAM, is associated with poor outcome in CRC, and that the expression of the three markers in combination has a stronger prognostic value.
the expression of Ald1, Survivins and EpCAM is an independent prognostic factor for survival and distant recurrence in CRC patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of these three markers is a strong prognostic factor for CRC patients.
the combination of Aldh1/Survivin/EpCAM expression is a powerful prognostic factor in colon cancer, but not in rectal cancer, which might be due to different tumour biology.
a combination of three markers, each representing a different cancer hallmark, is more powerful than single-marker expression for predicting survival and recurrence of colon cancer patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of three different biomarkers can be a strong prognostic indicator in colorectal cancer.

the combined analysis of biomarker expression levels, in this case for the main cancer hallmarks of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, cancer stemness, and tumour immune evasion, is a valuable approach to identify patients with poor clinical outcome.
the combination of biomarkers is a better prognostic indicator for survival and recurrence in colon cancer than single biomarkers.
